intro: Depression is a common, treatable illness, and because you see people daily you are well placed to notice changes and escalate concerns safely.
points: Any risk of self-harm or suicide must be taken seriously and escalated urgently; if in immediate danger, call 999.
Never promise to keep suicidal thoughts secret — be honest that you must share them to keep the person safe.
Depression is a treatable illness, not a weakness, so never tell someone to cheer up or pull themselves together.
Your role is to support, notice and report changes — not to diagnose or treat, which is a clinical decision.
Listen patiently and without judgement; warmth, a calm voice and unhurried time matter more than perfect words.
Record changes in mood, sleep, appetite or self-care factually, and report anything worrying promptly to the right person.
